subject.title: fix(agents): prefer native Windows PowerShell on PATH

question: Should OpenClaw standardize the shared Windows rule that any native `.exe` on PATH outranks an earlier extensionless shim for all extensionless shell lookups?
rationale: The implementation intentionally changes a compatibility-sensitive shared resolver rather than only the PowerShell-specific fallback; automated review can verify the mechanics and proof, but maintainers must accept the user-facing precedence policy.

options.title: Accept native executable precedence
options.body: Merge the PR with the documented `.exe`-only rule so PowerShell 7 and other directly launchable Windows shells are preferred over extensionless shims.

options.title: Narrow the policy to PowerShell
options.body: Request a PowerShell-specific repair if preserving earlier extensionless custom shims is more important than a shared resolver rule.

recommendation.title: Accept native executable precedence
recommendation.body: Merge the PR with the documented `.exe`-only rule so PowerShell 7 and other directly launchable Windows shells are preferred over extensionless shims.

likelyOwner.reason: The current change author documented the intended cross-caller policy and has the closest available evidence for the native Windows behavior.
